1.comment: Flat — single-line UI text where the container sets the height: buttons, pills, table cells. Unitless multiplier — line height = font size × 1. Figma resolves a bound line height as pixels, so text styles carry the equivalent percentage and these tokens are the reference and handoff value. Named with a hyphen because Figma rejects a dot in a variable name.

2.comment: Loose — long-form reading. Nothing uses it yet. Unitless multiplier — line height = font size × 2. Figma resolves a bound line height as pixels, so text styles carry the equivalent percentage and these tokens are the reference and handoff value. Named with a hyphen because Figma rejects a dot in a variable name.

1-25.comment: Tight — headings and display. Used by Title 18 and Display 28 (125%). Unitless multiplier — line height = font size × 1.25. Figma resolves a bound line height as pixels, so text styles carry the equivalent percentage and these tokens are the reference and handoff value. Named with a hyphen because Figma rejects a dot in a variable name.

1-5.comment: Normal — body copy and anything that wraps. Used by every 12, 14 and 16 style (150%). Unitless multiplier — line height = font size × 1.5. Figma resolves a bound line height as pixels, so text styles carry the equivalent percentage and these tokens are the reference and handoff value. Named with a hyphen because Figma rejects a dot in a variable name.
